A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoMa and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, limitations, and appendix material. All 12 pages of each version support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoMa benchmark results and ablations in Tables 2–4, plus representation and loss analyses in Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original CoMa benchmark results and analyses, including the revised pretraining-format results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The compression tokens, attention masking, QA pretraining, mean pooling, and contrastive learning procedure are unchanged. Table 3 relabels NTP as CE; cross-entropy was already specified in v1's Figure 1 and Section 6.4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining sources and 36 MMEB evaluation datasets across four task families, with 20 IND and 16 OOD datasets. The MMEB-V1 wording clarifies the benchmark name without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Benchmark baseline membership in Tables 2 and 4 is unchanged. Within Table 3, the comparison variants change: Single Turn (Split) disappears, and Description and Caption are listed separately.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises the reported pretraining-format controls by separately listing Description and Caption and dropping the scored split-dialogue condition. The 500K ablation sample budget, evaluation metric, splits, and main hyperparameters remain unchanged. This does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The format ablation in Table 3 changes its evidence about which supervision format best supports compression. The split-dialogue result is removed and separate description/caption results appear. Token-count sensitivity, token similarity, representation evolution, and loss-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The unchanged sampling of 100 instances for token-similarity analysis is not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 3 removes Single Turn (Split), averaging 64.9. The old Description scores reappear under Caption, averaging 65.2; v2 separately reports Description scores of 59.9/61.6/66.7/80.8, averaging 64.9. Their procedural relationship is unexplained, so this is not an established same-setting performance change. Tables 2 and 4 are unchanged. Section 4.2 adds a one-quarter-MoCa GPU requirement claim.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, InfoNCE objective, input serialization, and compression objective in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of decoupling compression from matching, efficient adaptation using limited data, automated QA synthesis, and competitive or state-of-the-art MMEB performance. Replacing VLM with MLLM in the abstract aligns terminology with the existing focus.

C2.justification: The explanations involving lossy compression, information coverage, token redundancy, and CE versus KL remain unchanged, as do the data-scale limitation and future modality discussion. Section 6.2 still discusses split-dialogue superiority despite removal of its result row.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the explicit configuration of 8×NVIDIA A800 (80GB) GPUs with a claim of requiring one-quarter MoCa's GPUs. This removes reproducibility detail without establishing a hardware change. Other implementation settings and the appendix generation prompt are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work discussion remain substantively unchanged. Section 4.2 adds a limited quantitative refinement to the efficiency positioning against the already cited MoCa: one-quarter its GPU requirements.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations, contact information, and corresponding-author markers; adjusts abstract terminology; lightly rewrites related-work prose; and removes the duplicated 'two stages' wording. Section order and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 is reformatted with revised row labels, CE terminology, an abbreviated average heading, and an updated highlighting caption. Tables 2 and 4 gain MMEB-V1 captions. Author-block changes and text reflow produce limited layout shifts; all figure contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Small gains in wording, Table 3 legibility, and additional format reporting are outweighed by removing the explicit GPU configuration and split-dialogue scores while retaining discussion of that comparison. The Description/Caption distinction also lacks procedural explanation. These changes slightly weaken reproducibility and evidential consistency; the core method and principal benchmark results remain intact.
